etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Medieval Latin accessōrius, from Latin accessor (“helper, subordinate”), from accessus. Compare access, from same root.

definitions.definition: Having a secondary, supplementary or subordinate function by accompanying as a subordinate; aiding in a secondary way; being additional; contributing or being contributory. [from 1550s][1]

quote.citation: 1641 May, John Milton, Of Reformation Touching Church-Discipline in England: And the Cavvses that hitherto have Hindred it; republished as Will Taliaferro Hale, editor, Of Reformation Touching Church-Discipline in England (Yale Studies in English; LIV), New Haven, Conn.: Yale University Press, 1916, →OCLC, 2nd book, page 48:
quote.text: Amongst many secondary, and accessory causes that support Monarchy, these are not of least reckning,  […]

definitions.definition: (law) Assisting a crime without actually participating in committing the crime itself; being connected as an incident or subordinate to a principal.
Present in a minor amount, and not essential.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English accessorie, from Medieval Latin accessōrius, from Latin accessor (“helper, subordinate”), from accessus. Compare access, from same root.

definitions.definition: Something that belongs to part of another main thing; something additional and subordinate, an attachment.

quote.citation: 1851, Thomas Carlyle, The Life of John Sterling, London: Chapman and Hall, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: the aspect and accessories of a den of banditti

definitions.definition: (fashion) An article that completes one's basic outfit, such as a scarf or gloves. [from 1896][2]

quote.citation: 2018 June 5, Jonah Engel Bromwich, Vanessa Friedman, Matthew Schneier, “Kate Spade, whose handbags carried women into adulthood, is dead at 55”, in The New York Times‎[1], New York, N.Y.: The New York Times Company, →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 6 June 2018:
quote.text: One of the first of a wave of American women contemporary designers who emerged in the 1990s, she [Kate Spade] built a brand on the appeal of clothes and accessories that made shoppers smile.

definitions.definition: (law) A person who is not present at a crime, but contributes to it as an assistant or instigator. [from 1414][4]

quote.citation: 2005, Jennifer Worth, Shadows of the Workhouse, Weidenfeld & Nicholson (2009), page 150:
quote.text: “You can be an accessory before the fact, or an accessory after the fact. It doesnʼt matter if itʼs before or after; either way youʼd be in for it.”

definitions.definition: (art) Something in a work of art without being indispensably necessary, for example solely ornamental parts.
